args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks (service unhealthy, error rate ~18%). The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. Mitigation: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release recorded as healthy in production. Follow-up: confirm recovery and investigate root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all production regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **What went wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. The service was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. The test build of v2.3.1 had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release marked healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions. Its earlier production record was healthy, so this didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Check after rollback:** The service now reports healthy, with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failed v2.3.1 deploy and the rollback. It also says to find the root cause in v2.3.1 before deploying it again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
